summary: Cadian presents itself in one paragraph as a fundamental, value-oriented global long/short equity manager at 'the intersection of tech and value', with a conservative net beta. The site is a legalistic one-pager with no team, AUM, performance or documents, aimed at LPs who already know the firm. It makes no AI, data or systematic claims and covers healthcare, industrials and consumer as well as TMT. Against TMS it is a discretionary generalist-leaning value shop, while TMS leads with a behavioural-sentiment quant overlay and a narrower tech/AI-hardware universe.

Atreides positions itself as a crossover investor bringing a long-term, private-equity-style perspective to technology and consumer companies across public and private markets. The site is almost empty apart from a large team directory, which signals institutional depth (IR, capital formation, ECM, ventures) rather than explaining a process. Its Form ADV shows a flagship hedge fund alongside many VC/PE vehicles, so its edge is public-private access, not a data or quant signal. TMS by contrast is purely liquid, public-equity tech long/short with a quantitative sentiment overlay and no private-market angle.

Alkeon markets 'two decades of investing in transformative companies' across their lifecycle and leads with a VC logo wall (Anthropic, Databricks, Stripe), with investor material behind a login. It reads as a growth/innovation crossover platform; long/short hedge funds dominate the ADV, but the brand story is private-company access. It also runs a UCITS fund and sub-advises registered funds, so it is not purely professional-only. Compared with TMS it competes on scale (USD 25bn regulatory AUM) and private deal flow, while TMS's angle is behavioural sentiment timing within liquid tech.

Sylebra's site now presents 'Sylebra Growth Partners', a growth equity firm writing USD 50-200M tickets across Platform, Growth and 'Private in Public' stages, with active board engagement. The low-net TMT long/short hedge fund behind its reputation is not mentioned at all; it appears only in Form ADV data as of end-2025, and regulatory AUM has fallen sharply. Its tone is aimed at founders and management teams, not hedge fund allocators. For TMS it is a weak direct comparable: if the hedge fund is being wound down or de-emphasised, Sylebra may fail the hard filter, and its positioning (engaged PE partner) is the opposite of TMS's liquid, signal-driven approach.

Whale Rock's public page is a two-sentence holding page: an SEC-registered Boston adviser investing globally with a TMT focus since 2006, plus a login tab and contact details. All substance (performance, letters) sits behind the login or reaches the market through press, e.g. Business Insider's monthly return leaks. Its line-up mixes the flagship long/short fund with long-only, MegaCap Tech and hybrid/private vehicles. Against TMS it is the scale TMT benchmark (about USD 13bn ADV) with no stated quant or sentiment component, so TMS's differentiation has to rest on its behavioural overlay and risk-appetite timing, not on tech focus alone.

TMS sits behind a 3-step country / investor-type / disclaimer gate, then presents itself as a long/short technology equity strategy combining fundamental picking with a quantitative sentiment and risk-appetite overlay. Unlike the peers it explains its process openly, but it shows no fund facts, AUM, performance, team or documents, and it does not set out the two sleeves (systematic since 2016, discretionary tech/AI since Dec 2025). The award is still labelled 'Managed Futures Newcomer of the Year 2023', which clashes with the L/S tech positioning. Peers reveal less but carry brand, scale or press coverage; TMS needs track-record and vehicle facts behind its gate to compete.
